predecessors.name: Saint-Domingue
predecessors.text: Saint-Domingue, the French colony in the west of Hispaniola, of which the slave rebels held the Northern Province ('By 1792, slave rebels controlled a third of Saint-Domingue')

successors.name: Republic of Haiti
successors.text: the same Haitian state under Cliopatria's third row, 'Republic of Haiti' 1936-2024

ledger.x: 1792: the slave rebels of Saint-Domingue hold the Northern Province.
1793: the British land in the west.
1794: the British take Port-au-Prince.
6 May 1794: Louverture joins the French and the revolutionary polity comes to stand for the whole colony.
1798: Maitland leaves the north-west.
1798: 'On 18 May the British left Port-au-Prince.'
June 1799: the War of the South begins.
11 March 1800: Toussaint takes Jacmel and Rigaud flees, so the whole colony is Louverture's.
1801: Louverture's constitution.
1801: Louverture takes Santo Domingo.
1802: the French take the east from Louverture's brother.
1802: the French expedition lands.
1803: the last French fall.
1 January 1804: Dessalines declares Haiti independent at Gonaïves.
22 September 1804: Dessalines becomes emperor; the First Empire of Haiti.
February 1805: Dessalines marches on the east.
March 1805: the siege is lifted.
17 October 1806: Dessalines is assassinated; Pétion becomes president of the southern Republic of Haiti.
October 1806: the north breaks away.
1820: Boyer reunites the north and south.
9 February 1822: Boyer enters Santo Domingo and unites the island.
27 February 1844: the east declares independence.
March 1844: Haiti tries to retake the east.
26 August 1849: Soulouque makes himself emperor, the Second Empire.
24 January 1856: the last Haitian invasion fails.
15 January 1859: Soulouque abdicates; the republic returns.
28 July 1915: US Marines land at Port-au-Prince.
1 August 1934: the occupation ends.
1935: bookkeeping end, not a political event.

wars.name: Haitian Revolution
wars.outcome: Rebel victory: the French lose the colony in 1803 (Vertières 18 November, evacuation 30 November) and Dessalines declares independence on 1 January 1804.

wars.name: War of the South
wars.outcome: Toussaint's victory: he took Jacmel on 11 March 1800, Rigaud fled, and Toussaint 'ruled Saint Domingue as its dictator'.

wars.name: Dessalines' invasion of Santo Domingo (1805)
wars.outcome: Failed: Dessalines took Santiago on 25 February, besieged Santo Domingo from 6 March and withdrew when French ships arrived; the east stayed outside the empire.

wars.name: Dominican War of Independence
wars.outcome: Dominican victory: separation of the Santo Domingo territory from Haiti; Haitian offensives of 1844, 1845, 1849 and 1855-1856 failed (Sabana Larga, January 1856).

wars.name: United States occupation of Haiti
wars.outcome: American victory over the Cacos (First Caco War ended with the capture of Fort Rivière on 17 November 1915; the Second, 1918-1920, with Batraville's death); the occupation ended 1 August 1934.

certainty.note: The rebel, French, British and Spanish zones of 1792-1803 and the line between Christophe's north and Pétion's south in 1806-1820 are approximate; the pages name no boundary.
The island entire, 'from Cape Tiburon to Cape Samana', bounded by the sea.
The Haitian-Dominican frontier is approximate until 1936 ('The frontier was not finalized until 1936'); the coasts are sharp.
